How this estimate works ＋

Alcohol (g) = volume (ml) × ABV / 100 × 0.789. Each completed drink adds alcohol / (weight × r) to the model. Between drinks, the estimate falls by 0.15‰ per hour and never below zero.

The other curves use 0.10 and 0.20‰ per hour. These are illustrative assumptions, not personal metabolism measurements or a guaranteed range. The model assumes instant absorption at completion and zero starting BAC; it cannot reproduce the absorption phase. Log all drinks. Food, body composition, medication, illness and individual variation are not modelled.

No “safe to drive” threshold is calculated. Zero is a mathematical projection, not a prediction you should use to decide when to drive.

Sources: NIAAA: metabolism · Hangovers and impairment · Jones: ethanol pharmacokinetics.
